items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: you could relate to Duke Ellington and Fats Waller and Fletcher Henderson in bands of that period

ctx.x: think in subsequent bands he, you know, used a lot of the influence of Duke Ellington and Charlie Parker.

Well, the influence -- the influence of Charlie -- of Duke Ellington is the basic -- the basis of the music that we played. So anything that you do is an influence of Duke Ellington. Charlie Parker went to a different level, modernized it, genius nevertheless, But it was a different -- a different mode of -- 'Black Lady' -- you could relate to Duke Ellington and Fats Waller and Fletcher Henderson in bands of that period, but -- and sit back and relax and listen to it.
But when Charlie Parker started with and Diz their's, you'd have to sit at the front of your seat to listen, which doesn't mean that you're relaxed. You're just a listener then.
